question: The mean of data is 56, and its median is 76. The mode (using empirical relation) of the data is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Empirical Formula**: **Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**.

Substitute the given values: **Mode** = 3(76) − 2(56).

**Mode** = 228 − 112 = 116.

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** of the data = 56

**Median** of the data = 76

**Formula Used:**

The **empirical relationship** between **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** is given by:

**Mode** = 3 × **Median** − 2 × **Mean**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4cbd7ded878b5d051fcbd141909ba4b6bda7430fba6521d6057274b5b8933793.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Mode** = 3 × 76 − 2 × 56

⇒ **Mode** = 228 − 112

⇒ **Mode** = 116

**∴ The correct answer is 116.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Empirical Relation

The formula **Mode** = 3 **Median** − 2 **Mean** is used for **moderately skewed** distributions.

Symmetrical Distribution

In a **perfectly symmetrical** distribution, the **Mean**, **Median**, and **Mode** are all equal (**Mean** = **Median** = **Mode**).

Skewness and Central Tendency

In a **positively skewed** distribution, **Mean** > **Median** > **Mode**. In a **negatively skewed** distribution, **Mode** > **Median** > **Mean**.</p
